Sample.evidence_source: "CFA was conducted on the 10 items of the BAS-2, where all items loaded onto a single latent variable. The standardised estimates of factor loadings for the best-fitting model were all good-to-excellent, with the exception of Items 1 and 9 which were fair (see Fig. 1). This one-dimensional structure provided an acceptable fit to the data: \chi_{\rm M}^2(32, N=345)=110.518, \chi^2_{normed} = 3.454, CFI = .953, RMSEA = .084 (low = .068, high = .102), SRMR = .047."

Number of studies.evidence_source: The section describes a single confirmatory factor analysis on the BAS-2 in one sample (N=345) and does not reference multiple studies or separate study labels.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a confirmatory factor analysis of the 10-item BAS-2 in a single sample (N=345), indicating a one-dimensional structure with generally good-to-excellent factor loadings (Items 1 and 9 were fair) and acceptable model fit (CFI = .953, RMSEA = .084, SRMR = .047). Multi-group analyses supported configural and loading invariance across sex and indicated intercept invariance, suggesting the BAS-2 structure is equivalent across male and female sub-samples. The text does not label the analysis as 'Study 1' or mention multiple distinct studies.
section_summary.evidence_source: "CFA was conducted on the 10 items of the BAS-2... This one-dimensional structure provided an acceptable fit to the data: \chi_{\rm M}^2(32, N=345)=110.518, \chi^2_{normed} = 3.454, CFI = .953, RMSEA = .084 (low = .068, high = .102), SRMR = .047." and "The unconstrained model had adequate fit for both sex sub-samples... suggesting configural invariance between the sexes... intercept invariance was evident, \Delta \chi^2(10) = 17.00, p = .074."
